title: ENDEX: 24-Hour Window Closed at IP-1 'Ridgeline Farm'

fields.resolution: ENDEX. It is 11:50 on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 on the exercise clock, four hours after STARTEX. In the story, it is Wednesday morning and the 24-hour window that opened with the 07:50 presumptive result has closed. The national reference laboratory has confirmed H5 HPAI at IP-1 'Ridgeline Farm', and all four barns are depopulated. This ends the exercise.
finalState: Ames confirmed H5 HPAI at IP-1 at 07:44 Wednesday. Barn 4 finished at 08:02, 12 minutes past the 24-hour goal.
Carcass loads are moving to the Calder County Regional Landfill and the Pell County Landfill, each under a Board movement permit on a set route.
The corrected county situation report matches the Board: one premises, 62,000 birds, a 10 km control area (federal planning value; the Minnesota plan governs) and 11 checkpoints.
The Board, APHIS and MDH continue to handle the permit queue, the Dunmore processing decision and worker monitoring.
The control area and checkpoints stay in place until the Board releases them. Recovery and checkpoint demobilization follow that release.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Please stop play now and put down your phones, radios and permit forms. We will take a ten-minute break and then start the hot wash here in the Training Room.
fields.hotWashMethod: Clock walk-back, then 3-Up, 3-Down: first, a timeline of the Annex K plan clocks from the 07:50 presumptive result. Then each table names three things that worked and three things that broke.
hotWashQuestions: Plan clocks: Which Annex K clocks did we meet and which did we miss: quarantine order, first four checkpoints, control area, all 11 checkpoints, notice, depopulation? What decision or missing resource set each one?

Permits and disposal: Why were feed permits PR-1014 and PR-1019 still on hold after 18 hours, and why did carcass trucks wait more than 12 hours at the landfill gate? What should be pre-arranged before the next presumptive result?

One set of numbers: How did '10 miles' get into SITREP #4, and what in our process would have caught it before the wire did? Did we call the Board's PIO before answering when the state and the cooperative used different figures?

Worker protection: Did every exposed worker, including the Catch Crew C members who speak K'iche', get counseling and an antiviral offer in their own language? How did we protect their health information when the employer asked for it?
Which decisions belonged to the Board, APHIS or MDH, and where did the county support them or start to make those decisions itself?
fields.facilitatorNote: Collect the EOC log, the permit desk printouts, SITREP #4 and the corrected SITREP before the break. Prompt the room to capture the plan's demobilization steps that follow the Board's release as action items, not discussion.

instructorNote: This card stops play and moves the room into the hot wash. It frames the discussion around the Annex K section 4 clocks measured from the 07:50 presumptive result, the permit and disposal backlog, consistent messaging under CCACMP section 10, and worker follow-up. Watch that players stop working the open items and that the demobilization steps after the Board's release are written down as action items.
